results.title: Godzilla
results.creator_credit: Roland Emmerich, Dean Devlin and Centropolis Pictures
results.brief_description: Perhaps one of the world’s most famous and enduring characters, Godzilla first appeared on Japanese screens in the 1954 release “Gojira”. In this version, the monster lizard has been created on a remote island somewhere in the South Pacific by nuclear testing, and she is heading to America, land of plenty, to hatch her offspring. Fantastic special effects make this the ultimate monster movie - a 20 story tall lizard with one thing on her mind.

results.title: Being John Malkovich [DVD]
results.creator_credit: Spike Jonze, Michael Stipe, Sandy Stern, Steve Golin, Vincent Landay, PolyGram and Propaganda Films
results.brief_description: Being John Malkovich is without a doubt one of the more surreal and original films to come out of America for some time. The inspired plot goes something like this, Craig Schwartz, a down on his luck puppeteer (John Cusack) takes on a filing job in a building on the 7 1/2 (the explanation why it’s 7 1/2 is hilarious). There, he encounters the sexy and cruel Maxine (Catherine Keener), whom he immediately forms an unhealthy attraction for, unbeknown to his timid and devoted wife, Lotte (an unrecognizable Cameron Diaz). Things get strange however when Craig discovers a small doorway at the back of a filing cabinet which ends up being a portal into John Malkovich’s mind. This of course is only the beginning. Director Spike Jonze, whose background is in music video’s (Beastie Boy’s “Sabotage” and Fat Boy Slim’s “Praise You” just to name a few) has opted to treat the film’s insane subject matter in the most matter of fact way. The screenplay by Charlie Kaufman explores every possibility that this existential conundrum evokes, at turns managing to be hilarious, weird and melancholy. Cast also includes Mary Kay Place, Charlie Sheen and Orson Bean.

results.title: Jason and the Argonauts [DVD]
results.creator_credit: Don Chaffey, Charles H. Schneer and Columbia Pictures
results.brief_description: Stemming from Greek mythology, this is the tale of the voyages of the intrepid Jason and his Argonauts on a quest to find the legendary Golden Fleece. He and his crew must brave all manner of dangers and face a host of terrifying foes, including the seven-headed Hydra, fighting skeletons, bloodthirsty Harpies and the invincible colossus Talos. It is also a tale of love, as the beautiful Medea risks everything for Jason and his quest. For its time, the special effects of Ray Harryhausen were given accolades by the critics. Stars Todd Armstrong as Jason and Nancy Kovack as Medea.

results.title: Bride of Chucky
results.creator_credit: Ronny Yu, David Kirschner, Grace Gilroy and Universal Pictures
results.brief_description: This is the fourth, and without a doubt the best in the controversial ‘Child’s play’ series. In the latest instalment Chucky (voiced supplied by Brad Dourif), the benevolent child’s toy is bought back to life in this inventive and witty sequel which plays more like a demented homage to ‘Bride of Frankenstein’. The sinister looking doll which is possessed by the evil spirit of a serial killer is resurrected from the dead by his unbalanced goth girlfriend (played with relish by Jennifer Tilly), who has wedding bells on her mind. However Chucky has more sinister intentions than marriage, when he and his trailer trash bride stow away with two runaway teens wrongly accused of murder. Hong Kong director Ronny Yu (‘Bride with the white hair’), and writer Don Mancini have fashioned a wonderfully irresponsible film which proudly wears it’s horror film references on its sleeve, giving the series some surreal, clever twists and turns. Cast also includes John Ritter, Alexis Arquette and Katherine Heigl.

results.title: Thunderbirds are go
results.creator_credit: David Lane, Sylvia Anderson and Associated Television (Overseas) Ltd
results.brief_description: The Tracy team launch a highly dangerous rescue mission in space in this first feature-length Thunderbirds classic. SZero X, a 21st century spacecraft, is suddenly blasted by a strange explosion as it leaves the Earth’s atmosphere bound for Mars. Is it sabotage? Can the Thunderbirds discover the perpetrators and save the next launch? This adventure film is gadget loaded and features visual effects by Derek Meddings as well as sound effects by some of London’s famous rock stars, including Cliff Richards.

results.title: The Great Muppet caper
results.creator_credit: Jim Henson, David Lazer, Frank Oz and ITC Entertainment
results.brief_description: Kermit and Fozzie Bear star as twin reporters, who together with the rest of the Muppet gang travel to Great Britain in search of jewel thieves. Catching the guilty culprits seems to be the only action to redeem themselves with their boss for letting the thieves escape under their very noses. During their stay Kermit meets Miss Piggy posing as fashion designer Lady Holiday (Diana Rigg), the woman whose gems have been stolen. While the Muppets are in Britain another of Lady Holiday’s diamonds is stolen and Miss Piggy is arrested on suspicion of theft. Now there is even more at stake than their jobs as the Muppets race to clear Miss Piggy’s name and stop another theft from occurring. Features cameos by Peter Falk, John Cleese, Peter Ustinov and others.

results.title: The Gold Rush (1925)
results.brief_description: The Gold Rush, an immortal classic, is regarded as one of Chaplin’s very best films, interweaving to brilliant effect the pathetic tale of the Tramp’s apparently hopeless love for a dancehall girl with the funny story of the Tramp and his burly gold prospecting partner heading off to make their fortunes in the great Yukon gold rush. Through the entire film hangs Chaplin’s finely perceived view of the contrast between the Tramp’s selfless, humanitarian behaviour, and the unpleasant, brutish life of the gold town society. Rated: G

results.title: Born in fire
results.creator_credit: Guy Baskin, Shepherd Baker Studios and Woodside Petroleum Ltd
results.brief_description: Depicts the final stages of construction, as well as the tow, launch and placement of the substructure for the first offshore production platform for the North West Shelf Project. The aim of the project is to develop a natural gas field to supply power for domestic and industrial use in Perth and southwest Western Australia. Narrated by John Waters. Suitable for secondary years 7-12.

results.title: Gerry Gee
results.brief_description:
Ron Blaskett helped bring ventriloquism from the stage to Victoria’s first television screens. Born in Melbourne in 1922, Blaskett became one of Australia’s best-known ventriloquists, adapting live puppetry for a new broadcast audience.

Blaskett and Gerry Gee made television history together on 11 October 1956, introducing GTV-9’s test program. Gerry’s name was inspired by ‘GTV’, and the pair later appeared on Channel 9’s opening night in January 1957. At a time when television was still finding its language, their partnership helped fill the screen with live character, humour and personality.

Made for Blaskett by Chicago puppet maker Frank Marshall, Gerry Gee could roll his eyes upwards and poke out his tongue. He became a favourite on The Tarax Show, inspiring merchandise including Gerry Gee Junior dolls. Blaskett and Gerry performed together for almost 60 years.

results.title: Adventure Island puppets
results.brief_description:
Adventure Island was a hugely popular ABC children’s television series, produced in Melbourne and screened five afternoons a week from 1967 to 1972. Created by Godfrey Philipp and John-Michael Howson, it grew out of The Magic Circle Club and followed stories set “far across the sea” in the Kingdom of Diddley-Dum-Diddley.

Puppets helped connect the fantasy world to the studio. Characters including Maxie Mouse, Samson the Cat, Crispian Cockatoo and Gracie Galah chatted with the host between story chapters, often sharing viewer drawings, riddles and jokes.

Built by Axel Axelrad, the puppets used different forms of operation. Samson was a large hand puppet, while the others were mechanical creations with rods inside or underneath the body to open the mouth or beak.
